```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(20261014)
```

## What is being tested, and whose hypothesis it is

Puangmalai et al. reported that tau aggregates from AD, PSP and DLB brain
recruit near-disjoint sets of protein partners, and proposed that different
folds expose different surfaces. **The hypothesis is theirs.** What follows is
a structural test of it, and should be framed that way in any abstract.

Null hypothesis: the accessibility of an interactor's tau-binding region in a
given disease's fold is unrelated to whether that interactor was actually
observed in that disease.

Two outcomes, both informative. If accessibility predicts the observed
pairings, fold geometry is sufficient to explain partner selection. If it does
not, PTMs and cofactors dominate over geometry.

## Inputs

```{r load-structural}
DATA <- "../data"

motif <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "motif_exposure.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
core  <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "core_matrix_long.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

folds <- core |>
  distinct(pdb_id, disease, fold_label, isoform) |>
  mutate(fold_id = sprintf("%s|%s|%s", disease, fold_label, pdb_id))

sprintf("%d folds across %d diseases", nrow(folds), n_distinct(folds$disease))
```

### The interactor table

Expected at `data/interactors.csv`, one row per interactor with a *published*
tau-binding region:

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `gene` | interactor gene symbol |
| `disease_observed` | disease whose aggregates recruited it; must match a `disease` in folds.csv |
| `region_start`, `region_end` | tau-binding region, 2N4R numbering |
| `region_source` | DOI or PMID for that region — the audit trail |

Interactors with no published binding region are **excluded**, not imputed.
That exclusion is itself a result worth reporting: it bounds how much of the
493 this analysis can speak to at all.

```{r load-interactors}
int_path <- file.path(DATA, "interactors.csv")
USING_SYNTHETIC <- !file.exists(int_path)

if (USING_SYNTHETIC) {
  # Placeholder so this document knits before the supplementary table is in
  # hand. Regions are invented. Every output below is labelled accordingly.
  interactors <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    disease_observed = unique(folds$disease),
    k = 1:6
  ) |>
    mutate(
      gene = sprintf("SYN%s%d", substr(disease_observed, 1, 2), k),
      region_start = sample(240:380, n(), replace = TRUE),
      region_end = region_start + sample(8:30, n(), replace = TRUE),
      region_source = "SYNTHETIC -- not a real binding region"
    ) |>
    select(gene, disease_observed, region_start, region_end, region_source)
} else {
  interactors <- read_csv(int_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

stopifnot(all(
  c("gene", "disease_observed", "region_start", "region_end", "region_source")
  %in% names(interactors)
))

if (USING_SYNTHETIC) {
  cat(strrep("=", 72), "\n")
  cat("SYNTHETIC INTERACTOR DATA. Every number below is meaningless.\n")
  cat("Place the real table at data/interactors.csv and re-knit.\n")
  cat(strrep("=", 72), "\n")
}

unmatched <- setdiff(interactors$disease_observed, folds$disease)
if (length(unmatched)) {
  warning("disease labels with no fold: ", paste(unmatched, collapse = ", "))
}

sprintf("%d interactors with a published region, %d diseases",
        nrow(interactors), n_distinct(interactors$disease_observed))
```

## Region exposure per fold

Exposure of a region in a fold is the fraction of its residues that are **in
the fuzzy coat and encoded by that fold's isoform**. Residues the isoform does
not encode are excluded from the denominator, not counted as exposed — the
same correction applied upstream, and the reason `core_state` is three-valued.

A region with no encoded residues in a fold yields `NA`, and those pairs are
dropped from the test with the count reported.

```{r exposure}
core_states <- core |>
  select(pdb_id, disease, fold_label, resno, core_state)

region_exposure <- interactors |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(
    gene = gene,
    disease_observed = disease_observed,
    region_start = region_start,
    region_end = region_end,
    core_states |> filter(resno >= region_start, resno <= region_end)
  ) |>
  group_by(gene, disease_observed, pdb_id, disease, fold_label) |>
  summarise(
    n_encoded = sum(!is.na(core_state)),
    n_total = n(),
    frac_exposed = if (n_encoded > 0) mean(core_state == 0, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(fold_id = sprintf("%s|%s|%s", disease, fold_label, pdb_id))

sprintf("%d gene x fold pairs, %d with no encoded residues (dropped)",
        nrow(region_exposure), sum(is.na(region_exposure$frac_exposed)))
```

```{r exposure-overview, fig.height=4}
ggplot(region_exposure, aes(frac_exposed)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "fraction of binding region in the fuzzy coat",
    y = "gene x fold pairs",
    title = "Distribution of region exposure across all fold-interactor pairs"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## The test

Statistic: mean exposure of each interactor's region in the folds of the
disease where it was observed, averaged first within disease (so a disease
with four deposited folds does not outvote one with a single fold), then
across interactors.

```{r statistic}
matched_statistic <- function(exposure, label_map) {
  # label_map: fold_id -> disease label used for matching
  exposure |>
    mutate(assigned = label_map[fold_id]) |>
    filter(!is.na(frac_exposed), assigned == disease_observed) |>
    group_by(gene, disease_observed) |>
    summarise(exposure = mean(frac_exposed), .groups = "drop") |>
    summarise(stat = mean(exposure), n_genes = n()) |>
    as.list()
}

true_map <- setNames(folds$disease, folds$fold_id)
observed <- matched_statistic(region_exposure, true_map)

sprintf("observed mean exposure = %.4f over %d interactors",
        observed$stat, observed$n_genes)
```

Null distribution: permute the disease labels across folds. This holds the
fold geometries, the interactor regions and the group sizes fixed, and breaks
only the correspondence between fold and disease — which is exactly the link
the hypothesis asserts.

```{r permute}
N_PERM <- 10000

perm_stats <- replicate(N_PERM, {
  shuffled <- setNames(sample(folds$disease), folds$fold_id)
  matched_statistic(region_exposure, shuffled)$stat
})

perm_stats <- perm_stats[!is.na(perm_stats)]
sprintf("%d of %d permutations yielded a statistic", length(perm_stats), N_PERM)
```

```{r result}
# Two-sided: the hypothesis predicts *selective* exposure, but the informative
# failure mode (partners bind where the fold is buried) is also a finding.
p_greater <- (1 + sum(perm_stats >= observed$stat)) / (1 + length(perm_stats))
p_less    <- (1 + sum(perm_stats <= observed$stat)) / (1 + length(perm_stats))
p_two     <- min(1, 2 * min(p_greater, p_less))

null_mean <- mean(perm_stats)
null_sd <- sd(perm_stats)

result <- tibble(
  observed = observed$stat,
  n_interactors = observed$n_genes,
  n_folds = nrow(folds),
  null_mean = null_mean,
  null_sd = null_sd,
  raw_difference = observed$stat - null_mean,
  standardised_effect = (observed$stat - null_mean) / null_sd,
  p_greater = p_greater,
  p_less = p_less,
  p_two_sided = p_two
)

knitr::kable(result, digits = 4)
```

```{r null-plot, fig.height=3.5}
ggplot(tibble(stat = perm_stats), aes(stat)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey80") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = observed$stat, colour = "#b2182b", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "mean matched exposure", y = "permutations",
    title = "Permutation null vs observed",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "red = observed (%.3f); null mean %.3f; two-sided p = %.4f%s",
      observed$stat, null_mean, p_two,
      if (USING_SYNTHETIC) "  [SYNTHETIC DATA]" else ""
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## Honest accounting

The brief is explicit: n is about 20 folds, so report effect sizes, run a
permutation test, and state the small n rather than dressing it up. No
classifier, no cross-validation. The numbers that bound the claim:

```{r accounting}
tibble(
  quantity = c(
    "folds analysed",
    "diseases with >=1 fold",
    "interactors in Puangmalai et al.",
    "interactors with a published binding region (used here)",
    "gene x fold pairs evaluated",
    "pairs dropped: region not encoded by isoform",
    "permutations"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(folds),
    n_distinct(folds$disease),
    493L,
    nrow(interactors),
    nrow(region_exposure),
    sum(is.na(region_exposure$frac_exposed)),
    length(perm_stats)
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Limits to state in the discussion rather than hope go unnoticed:

- **The fuzzy coat is not inert.** Treating it as uniformly accessible is a
  simplification. It is a polyelectrolyte brush whose compaction varies along
  the sequence and with phosphorylation, so "in the coat" is not the same as
  "available to bind". This is a real bound on the claim.
- **Published binding regions are coarse and biased.** They were mapped mostly
  on soluble monomeric tau, often by truncation, and they exist preferentially
  for well-studied partners. The subset with regions is not a random sample of
  the 493.
- **Resolution confounds the core/coat call.** Unresolved density is not only
  disorder: it also reflects local resolution and how far the depositors
  modelled. Test `frac_exposed` against entry resolution before claiming a
  fold difference.
- **One representative per fold is a choice.** Where several entries of one
  fold exist, re-running with a different representative is the cheapest
  robustness check available.

```{r resolution-confound}
# Requires a `resolution` column in folds.csv; carried through by step 2.
folds_csv <- file.path(DATA, "folds.csv")
if (file.exists(folds_csv)) {
  res <- read_csv(folds_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    select(pdb_id, resolution)
  conf <- region_exposure |>
    filter(!is.na(frac_exposed)) |>
    left_join(res, by = "pdb_id") |>
    group_by(pdb_id, resolution) |>
    summarise(mean_exposed = mean(frac_exposed), .groups = "drop")
  if (nrow(conf) >= 4 && n_distinct(conf$resolution) > 1) {
    print(cor.test(conf$resolution, conf$mean_exposed, method = "spearman"))
  } else {
    cat("too few folds for a resolution check\n")
  }
}
```
